categories.title: Roadmap step
criteria: Implements exactly the ROADMAP.md step named in the pull request title, and ticks its box in the same change
Every behaviour the step describes works through ./bin/malskill, not only inside a helper
Nothing the step asks for is missing, stubbed or left as a TODO

categories.title: Detection safety
criteria: Detection never gets weaker: no rule, pattern, fixture or test is removed, loosened or skipped, every malicious fixture still fires its rule, and the benign corpus still has zero findings
Rules still run on raw bytes; any file content shown to the user (terminal, Markdown, SARIF, JSON) is sanitised the same way: invisible unicode escaped, URLs defanged
No new subprocess outside malskill/explain.py, no network access, and no new path where a file the scanner could not read is dropped instead of reported as NOT-FULLY-ANALYZED

Nothing the default branch analyzes becomes NOT-FULLY-ANALYZED and no finding it reports disappears (that state exits 0, so it is weaker detection). A parsing, size-limit or discovery change adds a test: a hostile input main flags still gets that finding and exit 1

categories.title: Correctness
criteria: Exit codes hold: 0 no findings, 1 findings, 2 scanner error, unless the step changes them on purpose and says so
Every machine-readable output the change touches is valid (JSON parses, SARIF matches 2.1.0) and is tested
Odd input is handled without a crash: empty, unreadable or huge files, bad encodings, symlinks

categories.title: Tests
criteria: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests passes, and every new behaviour has a test in tests/
Tests cover real edge cases, not only the happy path, and fixtures needing special bytes (zero-width unicode, symlinks) are generated at test time
Tests use temporary directories and fixtures, never the developer's real home directory or the network

categories.title: Code quality and docs
criteria: Standard library only (no pip install, no yaml import), and it still runs on Python 3.9
Matches the code's existing style: small functions, the same naming, no dead code or duplicate helpers
README Commands section and docs/RULES.md or tests/README.md change where behaviour changed
